rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child's core argument: Federal aid is urgently needed, education must remain primarily under State control, Federal financial assistance is compatible with freedom from central control, and the Senate had already passed an aid bill. The child repeats this distinctive combination and adapts it to answer the committee's specific concern about the Office of Education and Federal Security Agency. C10 is also materially relevant to the child's separate administrative-reorganization discussion, but it is not as comprehensive a source for the letter as C01. C15 contains a related rebuttal of alleged Federal domination but concerns housing and is substantially weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I, too, am opposed to Federal control of the schools.... the control of education rests with the states.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Public provision for education has been primarily the concern of the several States, and must remain so. The maintenance of freedom of thought and expression depends in large measure upon keeping our systems of education free from central control.
shared_material.explanation: Both articulate the same central distinction between State control of education and permissible Federal involvement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Senate of the United States, when it passed a bill to provide for Federal aid to education, made it perfectly clear that it was opposed to Federal control of the schools
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A bill to provide Federal aid to education has recently been passed in the Senate by a substantial majority of both parties.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the earlier letter's legislative reference while adding the Senate bill's prohibition on Federal control.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The schools of the country are laboring under increasing burdens, and the need of Federal action to protect our children from the growing blight of poor and inadequate education is ever more pressing.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The cost of providing adequate systems of schools has long been beyond the financial resources of many of our States. Now a real crisis exists.... Unless the Federal Government comes to the aid of the States in meeting these needs, there is danger of a serious breakdown in our systems of education.
shared_material.explanation: The child condenses C01's factual and rhetorical case that inadequate State resources make Federal assistance urgent.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I sincerely hope that your Committee will soon complete favorable action on legislation of this character.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to express my earnest hope that the House of Representatives will take favorable action at this session upon legislation providing Federal aid for elementary and secondary schools.
shared_material.explanation: The letters share the same operative purpose and closely parallel concluding request for prompt favorable legislative action.
